newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-WIN GIVES ZELENSKAJA HOPE FOR WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIN GIVES ZELENSKAJA HOPE FOR WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Russian Warwara Zelenskaja eclipsed the favourites in a women's World Cup downhill on Saturday as Olympic champion Katja Seizinger crashed out.

The win, Zelenskaja's first of the season and only the second of her career, came on a downhill course skiers have likened to the Sestriere slope where they will contest the world title in two weeks' time.
As a consequence the 24-year-old Russian will now arrive at the world championships, which begin on Monday, ranked among the serious contenders for a downhill medal.
Olympic champion Seizinger is lucky to be going to the championships at all after suffering a spectacular crash near the end of her run.
Coming off a jump, Seizinger lost her balance. As she fought to regain control she caught the edge of her right ski in the soft snow and tumbled wildly off the course at 120 kph.
It was the first time the 24-year-old German had failed to finish a downhill since 1991 in Meribel.
But Seizinger, the defending overall World Cup champion, was unhurt.
"I only have a little headache," said Seizinger after skiing to the bottom of the hill. "I will race in the slalom tomorrow."
Capping a miserable day for the Germans, Miram Vogt also crashed out on the tricky, technical course but like Seizinger she escaped unscathed.
It was smooth sailing from top to bottom of the sun-bathed 2.6-km Fatschas course for Zelenskaja, who encountered no problems and posted a winning time of one minute 24.98 seconds.
"I knew right from the start of training that this was my type of slope," said the 24-year-old Zelenskaja. "Now I have confidence and I will take the next two weeks to get fit."
For the second straight weekend, Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen was forced to share her place on the podium. She tied for second with Austria's Renate Goetschl, both skiers clocking 1:25.07.
Last week Zurbriggen shared victory in Cortina d'Ampezzo with Italian Isolde Kostner.
"Another tie is fine with me, it's much better than having her go faster than me," said Zurbriggen.
The tie pushed American Hilary Lindh off the podium into fourth place with 1:25.30 and left Kostner, who had posted the fastest times all through training, in fifth with 1:25.32
Seizinger's crash will have severely dented her hopes of defending her overall title and of taking the downhill trophy this season.
Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, who finished 10th, strengthened her position at the top of the overall rankings and now lies 320 points ahead of Seizinger.
Seizinger slipped to third in the downhill rankings, 83 points behind Zurbriggen who leads with 349. In second place is Goetschl with 307.
Seizinger will be hoping to make up a bit of lost ground in Sunday's slalom here, which counts with the downhill for a combined competition.
